citations.quote: Title: A Phase 3 Study of Duvelisib (IPI-145) vs Ofatumumab in Patients with Relapsed or Refractory CLL/SLL
ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT02004522

Study IPI-145-07 was a randomized, open-label, actively controlled phase 3 trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of duvelisib compared to ofatumumab in 319 patients with relapsed or refractory CLL or SLL.

design.text: Randomized, open-label, actively controlled trial comparing duvelisib to ofatumumab; patients randomized 1:1.

citations.quote: Study IPI-145-07 was a randomized, open-label, actively controlled phase 3 study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of duvelisib compared to ofatumumab in patients with relapsed or refractory CLL or SLL. Patients were randomized 1:1

population.text: Adult patients with relapsed or refractory CLL or SLL after at least one prior therapy.

citations.quote: Efficacy in relapsed or refractory CLL/SLL is based on the results of a single, multicenter, open-label, randomized phase 3 trial (Study IPI-145-07) comparing duvelisib to ofatumumab in 319 adult patients with CLL/SLL after at least one prior therapy.
Diagnosis of CLL or SLL that meets at least one of the IWCLL 2008 criteria for requiring treatment

endpoint.text: Progression-free survival (PFS) per independent review committee (IRC).

citations.quote: The primary endpoint was progression-free survival as determined by independent review committee.
319 patients were randomized and included in the ITT population (160 subjects in the duvelisib arm and 159 patients in the ofatumumab arm)

result.text: Median PFS 13.3 months (duvelisib) vs 9.9 months (ofatumumab); HR 0.52 (95% CI: 0.39, 0.70); 1-sided log-rank p<0.0001. ORR 73% vs 45%.

citations.quote: median PFS of 13.3 months (95% CI: 12.1, 16.8)
median PFS of 9.9 months (95% CI: 9.2, 11.3), with a HR of 0.52 (95% CI: 0.39, 0.70; 1-sided stratified log-rank test p<0.0001)
ORR per IRC was statistically significantly higher for duvelisib (73%; 95% CI: 66, 80) than ofatumumab (45%; 95% CI: 38, 53)
Title: A Phase 2 Study of Duvelisib (IPI-145) in Subjects with Refractory Indolent NHL
ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT01882803

Study IPI-145-06 was a single-arm, open-label, phase 2 study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of duvelisib in patients with FL, marginal zone lymphoma (MZL), or SLL refractory to rituximab and chemotherapy combined or radioimmunotherapy.

design.text: Single-arm, open-label trial of duvelisib 25 mg twice daily in patients with FL, MZL, or SLL refractory to rituximab and chemotherapy or radioimmunotherapy; efficacy was analyzed in the FL subgroup.

citations.quote: Study IPI-145-06 was a single-arm, open-label, phase 2 study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of duvelisib in patients with FL, MZL, or SLL refractory to rituximab and chemotherapy combined or radioimmunotherapy.
All patients received duvelisib at a starting dose of 25 mg orally, twice daily in 28-day treatment cycles until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity.

population.text: Adult patients with FL refractory to rituximab and to either chemotherapy or radioimmunotherapy (efficacy analyzed in 83 FL patients).

citations.quote: included 83 patients with FL who were refractory to rituximab and to either chemotherapy or radioimmunotherapy (Study IPI-145-06)

endpoint.text: Overall response rate (ORR) per IRC per 2007 revised IWG criteria.

citations.quote: The primary endpoint is overall response rate as determined by independent review committee.
Overall response rate, with overall response defined as the best response of complete response or partial response, according to the 2007 revised IWG Criteria.
A total of 129 patients were enrolled and treated in the study, among which 83 patients (64%) with FL, 28 patients (22%) with SLL, and 18 patients (14%) with MZL.

result.text: In 83 FL patients, ORR per IRC 42% (95% CI: 31, 54), 1 patient (1%) CR and 34 patients (41%) PR.

citations.quote: The analysis of ORR per IRC in the 83 patients with FL demonstrated an ORR of 42% (95% CI: 31, 54), with 1 patient (1%) achieving a complete response and 34 patients (41%) achieving a partial response.

indication.text: COPIKTRA is a kinase inhibitor indicated for adult patients with relapsed or refractory CLL or SLL after at least two prior lines of systemic therapy (current label). At original NDA approval it was also granted accelerated approval for relapsed or refractory FL after at least two prior systemic therapies.

citations.quote: COPIKTRA is a kinase inhibitor indicated for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) or small lymphocytic lymphoma (SLL) after at least two prior lines of systemic therapy. (1)
Accelerated approval for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma (FL) after at least two prior systemic therapies.

target_moa.text: Duvelisib is a phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) inhibitor with dual activity against the PI3K-delta and PI3K-gamma isoforms, which play key roles in the proliferation and survival of malignant B cells.

citations.quote: Duvelisib is a phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) inhibitor with dual activity against the PI3K-\delta and PI3K-\gamma isoforms.
The B-cell receptor (BCR) and PI3K play key roles in the proliferation and survival in CLL/SLL

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=20%): diarrhea or colitis, neutropenia, rash, fatigue, pyrexia, cough, nausea, upper respiratory infection, pneumonia, musculoskeletal pain, and anemia. Serious, including fatal, infections occurred in 31% of patients; treatment-related mortality occurred in 15%.

summary.text: COPIKTRA (duvelisib) received regular approval for relapsed/refractory CLL or SLL after at least two prior therapies and accelerated approval for relapsed/refractory FL after at least two prior systemic therapies, under priority review, with orphan drug designations for CLL/SLL and FL.
